status: DONE. `gov accept` now reads the map, and all six KPI lines appear in its `lines`.
work_completed: Fixed the two rows that named no numbered KPI line. The interface row now starts "K1, K2, K4:" (the lines the `seed` answer and the `stores.json` record serve). The failure row now starts "F1 (the ticket's first failure line):" and lists the tests by name instead of the bare `assert_same_store`. I fixed a third defect `gov accept` would have hit: the K2 row's item `test_…_runs_cold[code, schema, embedder-model, embedder-revision]` counts as naming a test (it starts with `test_`) but matches no test as a bare word, so K2 would have failed as "missing". It is now the bare function name, with the four cases in plain words. I also took the backticks off two words in the K4 row that aren't tests (`~/gov-os-worktrees/W2-00-store`, `HOME`). No test and no expectation changed.

It exited 3 with `ok: true` and outcome `fail`, as expected on the base code. Per line (passed/failed): success-1 1/9, success-2 1/10, success-3 0/1, success-4 1/7, success-5 1/3, failure-1 0/10. Unmapped 0/0/0. Totals 2 passed, 24 failed, the same red as batch 1.
discoveries: `gov accept` counts a backticked item as naming a test when it contains `::` or starts with `test_`. If such an item matches no collected test, its line fails as missing. So a function name with parameter ids in brackets breaks a line: name the bare function, or `file.py::test_x[id]` for one case.
risks: A file item (such as `test_w2_122_answer_and_record.py`) maps every test in that file to its row's lines. That is intended here: each file serves the lines its row names.
lessons: Before committing a README map, run `gov accept` (or `gov.accept.runner.parse_map`) on it.
proposed_decisions: none. P-W2-122-TD-1 and TD-2 from batch 1 are still with the lead.
